items._cn_summary: Camille Norment 的作品被定位为实验艺术的代表，强调好奇心与反思的空间，与当代社会、文化和政治形成对话，但不强加说教意图。文章指出她的创作提供一种具身化的体验，听众会在之后的数日、数周乃至数月里反复回味，解析其与个人经验的共鸣。文本明确提及"sound"（声音）作为核心元素，暗示这是一部以声音艺术为导向的作品，但正文片段在介绍专辑具体音乐手段与结构之前便已截断，未能展开技术细节或曲目分析。文章整体偏向艺术评论式的概括，未深入讨论具体的声响设计、乐器编制或录音手法，信息密度偏低，但所描述的方向与实验艺术、当代声音创作的语境高度契合。

items.body: Review by martindavey87 — I can't really dwell on this one for too long, it pretty much is what it says it is. Most of these songs are demos and as such, the quality reflects that. Although, they're fun to hear the progress of the writing, especially with 'Inferno', where vocalist Russell Allen replaces unfinished lyrics with a random "do do dooooo" (just as you're getting into it and preparing to belt out the actual lyrics at the top of your voice!). And then of course, there's the 'Star Wars Suite' and a demo of the unreleased track 'Disillusioned'. 'Disillusioned' is a decent track which would have fit perfectly on the bands' first album, and the Star Wars song, well, is what it is. I love Symphony X, and if you're a die-hard fan like me, this is actually a very cool disc (especially since there's some dodgy unofficial versions floating around now, which admittedly does have much better artwork), and while it's nothing you'd ever really choose to listen to more than a couple of times, it's still a worthy addition to the collection.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑收录了Symphony X的demo与稀有录音，包括未发行曲目《Disillusioned》和《Star Wars Suite》。其中《Inferno》的demo版里，主唱Russell Allen在未完成歌词处用随意的“do do dooooo”代替，能听到创作过程中的即兴状态。整体录音质量明显是粗糙的demo水准，但可以借此观察歌曲从草稿到成型的演变。《Disillusioned》被认为是一首质量不错的作品，风格接近乐队首张专辑。乐评指出，这些内容对铁杆粉丝有特殊吸引力，尤其考虑到市面流传的盗版版本，这张官方合集更具收藏意义，但普通听众可能只会听一两遍。作为前卫金属乐队的文献性发行，它提供了了解乐队早期构思的窗口，而不是一张适合反复聆听的正式专辑。

items.body: Review by alainPP — Cambrian evokes Symphony X and Dream Theater, blending progressive metal and death metal with screamed vocals."What Lies Beneath - Pt. 1" opens with the sound of surf, Gregorian whispers, and a dark, vulnerable spoken-word passage. Crystal-clear piano, high-pitched vocals, and a solemn tone set the cinematic stage. "Rules of Engagement" explodes with heavy drums driving feverish keyboards; Epica-style growls meet Freek's snarling vocals, while the rhythm section allows for both intense passages and melancholic, My Dying Bride-esque moments featuring a solemn organ of despair. A highlight is the delicate piano outro accompanied by a distressed, screaming vocal. "Locked Room Murder Mysteries" begins with arpeggios before unleashing screamed vocals over neo-prog keyboards?a successful blend. This multi-layered fusion of heavy aggression and swirling keyboard work makes one forget the story's cruelty. There's a sudden hint of Anathema; the vibe is a plus, though the nasal vocals are a downside, wavering between melody, doom, and restrained violence."Requiem for Innocence" serves as an atmospheric intermezzo driven by emotional piano; the swelling melodic crescendo paves the way for the dramatic "Oceans Away," featuring razor-sharp riffs, machine-gun percussion, and fiery keyboards layered with a Balkan accordion. Lennart's class shines through in this track?at once festive and cruel?a melancholic folk ode set against a djent backdrop, featuring a solo reminiscent of Jordan Rudess and a spine-tingling keyboard-guitar duel."Shards of a Broken Mirror" channels Dream Theater with its musical opulence and richness. Freek drives the narrative forward as the instruments flood the senses with progressive metal that?with its extreme growls?bears the unmistakable scent of Opeth. The fusion might unsettle purist prog fans, yet the solemn keyboard-and-vocal breaks serve as a reminder that the prog spirit runs deep. A long, atmospheric acoustic outro gives way to the sudden arrival of "Last Man Standing"?cut from the same cloth, featuring grand, soaring keyboards set against metronomic drumming. The sound is both ominous and divine, an all-encompassing "liturgical metal" experience; the languid vocals?hovering between singing and narration?evoke Light Damage, while the sacred fire, double-kick drumming, and layered growls bring Epica to mind. A vehement track, dripping with narrative drama and neoclassical keyboards, reminding us that beneath every metalhead lies years of music theory training. "Requiem for Guilt" unfolds toward the finale, with spoken vocals drifting over airy keyboards before a powerful surge?a razor-sharp riff cutting through luminous synth lines. The atmospheric fusion, enhanced by a piano break, crystallizes the mood; tension builds like a lava-filled crater awaiting an imminent eruption. An Anathema-style finale follows, offering gentleness alongside a fleeting guitar solo. "What Lies Beneath - Pt. 2" brings the story to a close?sometimes, is it better not to reveal the truth? A melancholic, atmospheric finale turns the final page.Cambrian spent eight years crafting this album, a blend of neoclassical passages, growls, and progressive, atmospheric, and doom-laden breaks; it is classic, sprawling progressive metal?though its tendency to pack in too many ideas proves to be its Achilles' heel. (3.5)

items.body: Ultravox, the British new wave and electronic band, released “Systems of Romance” on 8 September 1978 through Island Records. The album turns 48 this year. It was the group’s third studio album, the first credited without the exclamation mark the band had carried since its debut, and the last to feature original singer and lyricist John Foxx. The band recorded it at Conny’s Studio near Cologne, West Germany, with Conny Plank and Dave Hutchins co-producing alongside Ultravox. Guitarist Stevie Shears was dismissed in early March 1978 and replaced by Robin Simon, whose only Ultravox album this is. The line-up was completed by Chris Cross on bass, synthesizer and vocals, Billy Currie on keyboards and violin, and Warren Cann on drums, rhythm machine and vocals. Electronics carried more of the record than on either of the two previous albums: synthesizer bass replaced conventional bass on several tracks, “Quiet Men” used a Roland TR-77 rhythm box in place of drums, and “Dislocation” and “Just for a Moment” dropped acoustic and synthetic drums entirely in favour of treated ARP Odyssey sounds. Cann later described the opening track to interviewer Jonas Warstad as the point where the two halves of the band’s sound met: “it perfectly represented our amalgamation of rock and synthesizer, many of the ideas and aspirations we had for our music gelled in that song”. The ten-track album runs “Slow Motion”, “I Can’t Stay Long”, “Someone Else’s Clothes”, “Blue Light”, “Some of Them”, “Quiet Men”, “Dislocation”, “Maximum Acceleration”, “When You Walk Through Me” and “Just for a Moment”. Island issued “Slow Motion” as a single on 11 August 1978 and “Quiet Men” on 20 October 1978, book-ending the album. The band had already played early versions of both at the Reading Festival on 27 August 1978. Neither single nor the album entered the UK charts. Sales figures differ by source: the 2006 reissue sleeve notes give over 20,000 copies, while Wikipedia’s Ultravox entry cites initial sales of over 25,000. Foxx has explained the title as a borrowing from Plank’s working method and his interest in systems music. “I liked the idea of intangible emotional elements running through mathematical frameworks,” he said. “It seemed a perfect encapsulation of the spirit of the music I was attempting to get to at that moment.” No song of that name appears on the album; Foxx recorded one for his 1981 solo album “The Garden”. British reviews split. In Sounds on 2 September 1978, John Gill rated the album four out of five and wrote: “Whatever anyone says, Ultravox (sans ‘!’) have always been that important step ahead of fashion… Personally I don’t think it’s their best (album) but the deftly alienating production and the tricky use of electronics make it an important enough development in the career of a band that always aims for the unusual”. Island dropped Ultravox on 31 December 1978. The band financed a US tour itself in early 1979, and at its end in March Foxx announced he would leave to work solo, handing the remaining members the band name. He had decided as early as the first Systems of Romance rehearsals, he told Vice in 2013. Simon stayed on in the United States. Currie was recruited that same year by Gary Numan, who has named the 1970s Ultravox as the most important influence on his music, first for a Tubeway Army appearance on The Old Grey Whistle Test and then to play on Gary Numan’s ‘The Pleasure Principle’ and its tour. Cross, Currie and Cann later recruited Midge Ure, who wrote in his 2004 autobiography that he “loved that album”, and whose reconstituted line-up played Systems material live with Ure singing Foxx’s lyrics. About Ultravox Ultravox formed in London in April 1974 as Tiger Lily, on the initiative of Royal College of Art student Dennis Leigh, who later took the name John Foxx. Chris Allen, later Chris Cross, played bass and Stevie Shears guitar; Warren Cann joined on drums in May 1974 and Billy Currie on violin that October. The group released one single as Tiger Lily in 1975 and went through several further names before signing to Island Records in 1976 and settling on Ultravox! in October that year, the exclamation mark a reference to Neu!, another Conny Plank production. Island released the debut “Ultravox!” in February 1977, co-produced by Steve Lillywhite and Brian Eno, and “Ha! Ha! Ha!” later the same year. Neither charted. The closing track of the second album, “Hiroshima Mon Amour”, used a Roland TR-77 drum machine and pointed towards the direction the band took next. “Systems of Romance” moved that balance towards electronics, working with Conny Plank, who had produced Kraftwerk‘s first four albums. After Island dropped the band and Foxx left in 1979, Foxx recorded the electronic solo album “Metamatic” (1980) and then “The Garden” (1981), which revisited the Systems-era material with Robin Simon on guitar; Side-Line covered the complete ‘Cathedral Oceans’ vinyl boxset drawn from his later work in 2016. Cross, Currie and Cann continued with Midge Ure on vocals, guitar and keyboards, signing to Chrysalis Records. “Vienna”, released in July 1980 and again produced by Plank, reached number 3 in the UK on the back of its title single, which peaked at number 2 in early 1981. Ultravox’s ‘Rage in Eden’ followed in 1981, recorded once more at Plank’s studio, then “Quartet” (1982) with George Martin producing, “Lament” (1984) and “U-Vox” (1986). Cann was dismissed before the U-Vox sessions, and the band split after that album’s tour in 1987. Currie reformed Ultravox with new singers for “Revelation” (1993) and “Ingenuity” (1994) before dissolving it again in 1996. Cann, Cross, Currie and Ure reunited in 2008, toured from 2009 and released the studio album “Brilliant” on 28 May 2012; their last show was at London’s O2 Arena on 30 November 2013. Chris Cross died on 25 March 2024, aged 71, as Side-Line reported in Ultravox musician Chris Cross dies aged 71. Chrysalis issued “The Collection (Deluxe Edition)” in December 2025, and Richard Evans published a band biography discussed in Richard Evans on Ultravox. Forty-eight years on, “Systems of Romance” remains the record where the Foxx line-up put its synthesizers at the centre, months before the band that made it came apart.

items._cn_summary: Ultravox 1978年发行的《Systems of Romance》是乐队去掉了名称中的感叹号后的首张专辑，也是原主唱John Foxx参与录制的最后一张作品。录制地点选在西德科隆附近的Conny Plank工作室，由Plank与Dave Hutchins联合制作，电子元素在该作中的占比明显高于前两张专辑：合成器贝斯取代传统贝斯出现在多首曲目中，Roland TR-77节奏机替代鼓机，ARP Odyssey处理后的音色被用于替代原声与合成鼓声。鼓手Warren Cann曾指出，开篇曲凝聚了乐队将摇滚与合成器融合的核心追求。Foxx将专辑标题解释为对Plank系统音乐工作方式与数学框架中流淌的情感元素的致敬。尽管英国乐评反应分化且销量与单曲均未进入榜单，该作在暗潮与电子音乐发展脉络中具有承前启后的位置。

items.body: Northern Irish composer Hannah Peel will release her original score for “Underland” on CD on 16 October via Rivertones, followed by a world premiere performance of the score at the Barbican on 24 October as part of the “Hannah Peel: In Focus” two-day series. “Underland” is Peel’s score for Robert Petit’s film adaptation of Robert Macfarlane’s book of the same name. The album combines synthesizers with ancient Mayan pod trumpets and an Iron Age horn called a carnyx, alongside baroque choir and string orchestra. Peel said she read Macfarlane’s book in 2019 and had already used some of its words on her 2022 album “The Unfolding,” calling the chance to score the film itself “beautiful synchronicity.” She described the project as scoring for “these astronauts of the underworld, those sacred ancient cave systems,” and said combining “mythology, technology and possibility” was central to the record. The CD tracklist runs 18 tracks, including “Into the Underland,” “Xibalba,” “Seeing in the Dark,” “The Waiting Wonder,” “You Don’t See Sunlight,” “The Earth Doesn’t Forget,” and “The Ascent.” The Barbican premiere, adapted for stage by Kieran Brunt, will be performed by contemporary vocal ensemble Shards with imagery from the film adapted by director Robert Petit. It forms the second half of “Hannah Peel: In Focus,” which opens on 23 October at Milton Court with “PIA,” a new live production of her 2020 album “Mary Casio: Journey to Cassiopeia,” created with choreographer Katya Bourvis and creative producer Tala Lee-Turton and scored for a 17-piece brass band. The 24 October date also includes a performance of “The Endless Dance,” Peel’s recent album with percussionist Beibei Wang on Real World Recordings. Peel and Beibei Wang will also play the Glasshouse International Centre for Music in Gateshead on 20 October and St Luke’s in Glasgow on 21 October. About Hannah Peel Hannah Peel is a Northern Irish composer, producer, and broadcaster whose work often connects science and music. Her studio albums include “Mary Casio: Journey to Cassiopeia” (2017), scored for synthesizers and colliery brass band; the Mercury Prize-nominated “Fir Wave” (2021); “The Unfolding” (2022) featuring the Paraorchestra; and “The Endless Dance” (2026) with Beibei Wang. Peel received an Emmy nomination for her score on “Game of Thrones: The Last Watch” and has since scored “Scoop” (Netflix), “Bring Them Down” (Mubi), “Midwinter Break” (Focus Features), and the horror film “Saccharine.” Her electronic score for “The Midwich Cuckoos” (Sky) won the Ivor Novello Award for Best Television Soundtrack in 2023, making her the first solo female composer to win that award. Peel also presents BBC Radio 3’s “Night Tracks.” “Underland” continues her run of film and stage work, following its “beautiful synchronicity” with a book she had already drawn on for “The Unfolding.” You Don’t See Sunlight by Hannah Peel

items._cn_summary: 北爱尔兰作曲家Hannah Peel为Robert Macfarlane同名书籍的电影改编版创作原声专辑《Underland》，将合成器与玛雅pod号角、铁器时代的carnyx铜管、巴洛克合唱团及弦乐团并置，形成跨越古代声响与电子技术的独特编配。专辑共18首曲目，主题围绕洞穴深处的"地底宇航员"展开，融合神话、科技与未知可能性。作品由当代人声 ensemble Shards在巴比肯艺术中心世界首演，配以导演Robert Petit改编的影像。作为In Focus系列活动的一部分，还包括与铜管乐队合作的《Mary Casio》现场版及与打击乐家Beibei Wang的合作演出，Peel此前曾以《The Midwich Cuckoos》获艾弗·诺韦洛奖，展现其在当代配乐与跨领域创作中的成熟经验。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — I'm a sucker for flashy weird cover art which in this case features some sort of giraffe-necked girlin the company of cyan backed stripes and bubble curlers. Add some wily angularity of classicUnivers Zero or Present based avant-prog and my interest is peaked. The Seattle based TROOT emergedfrom the band's namesake Tim Root who assembled a fiery chamber prog band that consists of 10musicians and takes a journey through the crossroads of classic chamber prog, avant-jazz and freeimprovisation. The band released its so far one off CONSTANCE AND THE WAITING in 2018 with anensemble that was handpicked from some of the most demanding and obscure underground acts in theranks of the experimental music universe.Root is the head honcho here and began his career as a classically trained pianist therefore thepresence of his piano-based charm is a dominant force throughout this album's six tracks with a 411/2 minute run. With 10 players on board this is the wonderful world of controlled chaos with theusual rock instrumentation of two guitarists, two bassists and a drummer along with the skronkyeffects of a saxophone and the expected chamber part of the equation in this case delivers by meansof the violin however there are ample offerings of an accordion adding some Mediterranean cafeelegance to the mix. While the star of the show is Root and his keyboard charming antics, the restof the band is quite competent delivering raucous avant-prog uprooting with the first two tracks"Axe For The Frozen Sea Within" and "Dance Elena" running the gamut of time signature frenzies atbreakneck speed to eerie atmospheric breakouts.While the album starts off on a high note, Root unfortunately steers things into a more pianorecital type of number on "Palasidai" which slows down the tempo and feisty knotty workouts severalnotches and rather serves as a breather that bucks the trend of atonal dissonance in favor of a moreballady even melodic piece that sounds a bit out of place although not bad per se. "Venice Of TheSky" jumps back into the avant-prog mind [%*!#]ery with stronger doses of jazz added to the mix andthe missing energy oomf that was missing from the previous track. And then another rather sleepyballad type of piano-based track with "Hollow By Footsteps" which sounds more like a 1950s jazzballad than anything that belongs on this album and IMHO the weakest track of the lot even if notbad if included under a different album mood setting. The album is redeemed by the knotty closer"Joey" which reverts back to the UZ meets Art Zoyd on steroids playbook and generates a scorcher ofan ending.Overall not a bad album save the two tracks that derail the momentum. Despite the furor of nastyavant-prog crafted on this album, the band unfortunately sounds a bit too close to its influencestherefore not really standing out as something unique and innovative although the band's excellentmusicianship makes this a very compelling listen nonetheless. It's not a perfect album due to thetwo lesser tracks that water down the whole album effect but even those tracks are not offensivelyawful in any way, just not suitable for what would make a cohesive album experience for me. Whilenot anything new under the sun at this point, the musical outfit known as TROOT nevertheless derivesan above competence level of crafty Rock In Opposition styled avant-prog that navigates an all-instrumental trajectory at least until the frenetic and unexpected screaming at the end of "Joey"which adds a nice twist to the tale. I do very much this band returns with a more adventurous albumbut despite the flaws this is still a very pleasant nerd out for those of us who love thisadventurous prog exhibitions of grandeur.

items._cn_summary: TROOT是一支来自西雅图的实验性前卫乐队，由钢琴家Tim Root领衔，集合了十名乐手，涵盖两把吉他、两把贝斯、鼓手、萨克斯、小提琴与手风风琴。这张专辑在古典室内乐、avant-prog与自由即兴之间穿梭，开篇两曲以密集的拍号变换与噪音张力开场，呼应Univers Zero与Art Zoyd的凌厉风格。然而中段两首钢琴ballad被乐评认为拖慢节奏、削弱整体动力，结尾曲目重新回到高能即兴作为弥补。乐评整体肯定其演奏水准与编制野心，但也指出乐队尚未脱离前辈影响，独特性不足。对于喜爱avant-prog与前卫即兴融合的听众而言，这是一张技艺扎实但风格定位尚在摸索的作品。

items.body: Review by tszirmay — Well, this album certainly pertains to the title, finding beauty and truth in musical form is a luxury that progressive rock can easily provide. Back in 2020 when leader Dave Bandana began this project, he immediately connected with some exemplary musicians, names like Peter Jones (surely one of the great British prog talents), American drummer Tim Gehrt, Welsh guitarist Gareth Cole and the illustrious Cosmograf Robin Armstrong (who left after the second album). The four mentioned though are still the core, firmly entrenched in heir own little universe, crowning their relationship with this splendid effort, as well as being their finest. Toss in wordsmith Brad Birzer, and the sterling lyrics come alive with profound poignancy. Nice expansive track to launch the listening experience, "Islands" has all the classic ingredients to make one lose themselves in an atoll of sonic pleasure. A heady combination of various stylistics seamlessly concocted to create escapism at its finest. Orchestral, Celtic, jazz, rock and folk tendencies unite as a common front, without any kind of tedium or overt simplicity. Initially silky smooth and ambient, the drama takes little time to divulge its many enjoyments, Gehrt's primal beat bashing along like a giant wave, Cole's tingling guitar behaving like a rudder, all captained along by Mr. Jones' exceptional storytelling voice. Like a sudden monsoon surging across the horizon, the latter's saxophone skills inject a sunny luminescence that can only make the heart race a tad faster. When the 'timeless' brass and axe decide to interweave, well, it is called magic for a reason! There goes my jaw again, fluttering away in the wind! I mean , WOW! Only a breezy pseudo-instrumental can express the willowing beauty of "Fallen Leaves", the numerous choral voices acting like foliage swept by Newton's discovery. Its brief yet arching voluptuousness and fragile pastoral sense evokes images of acceptance and serenity. An ideal set-up for the colossal wallop of "Arribabok", the suave Bandana bass underwrites the complete array of sophisticated sounds emanating from each instrument, proposing an almost funky vibe, yet Cole does experiment with Manzanera-like slivers from his insistent guitar and Jones does an extended Andy Mackay move on the saxophone. One can even detect a Paul Thompson sense on the drum kit. Proggy Roxy (my highest possible compliment)! Much like my very best friend Lazland, my favourite month is also October, being hopeless romantic Autumn fans me thinks, and on "October Sun", it's purely heartwarming in its utter innocence, verging on panacea for the soul of fall worshippers, 'until the sun shines through'. A hint of my all-time favourite album (Hero and Heroine by the Strawbs), what with choral mentions of shining and suns, the clanging Cole guitars even recollect fond memories of Dave Lambert. Thankfully, the Jones saxophone slams this into another jurisdiction as the jovial bass bops like a Mexican jumping bean (remember those?). My feet, my hands and my head were forcefully keeping the beat?.Fun times coming up soon . Speaking of which, "From Empty Trees" has a monstrous and trebly bass running rampant on this instrumental, the ebullient synthesizers slipping between the branches, organ unafraid to pomp as well as supply ceremony and finish of the proceedings with a scorching guitar solo just to keep the forest ranger faraway from Yogi Bear (let us not forget Bubu). Epic time to rejoice once again, "A View" offers an orchestral and rhythmic foundation for Jones to emote vocally like only he can. His ability to plead, to beg, to steal and to borrow in his various inflections is absolutely masterful. Every single vowel and consonant are clear as the water in that lagoon on that island, where this stellar journey began. Talk about escapism, I have been somewhere else since the very first note, very track a joyful paradise. "Harder to See" is next and it's hard to imagine that the overt atmosphere keeps glowing like a spiritual fireball , 'I sit and wonder! You have a plan and you can', believe you me! An inquisitive sentiment on the complexity of confusion, of misdirection, of illusion, call what you want, its only words. The lamenting backing harmony vocals showcase the despair. Being a prog archivist and having a ramrod strong memory of all my hundreds of concerts , "Rewind" seems to wander back to gentler times, as befits us old geezers who still feel comfort in a youth very well lived. There is quite the classic golden age of 70s Prog feel to this finale , a carefree time when labels were meaningless and overt criticisms wiped away by astonished eyes and ears, every occasion we walked into a record store or a concert hall. Even the smells remain vivid to this day. The empowering orchestral send-off with acoustic guitars, flutes and mellotrons in tow is plain orgasmic. Rael must be on a poster somewhere in the studio, its eerie and yet so utterly expressive. Perhaps it was due to the Fly on the Windshield. 5 faultless things definitely worth remembering (who, what, where, when and why)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是英国跨界前卫摇滚乐队在2026年的回归之作，核心阵容由贝斯手Dave Bandana领衔，集合了键盘/歌手Peter Jones、鼓手Tim Gehrt与吉他手Gareth Cole。评论者用大量感官化语言描述其编排，如开篇曲融合管弦乐、凯尔特、爵士、摇滚与民谣元素，萨克斯与吉他的交织被形容为魔幻时刻。中段曲目带有Roxy Music式的优雅funk律动和Strawbs式的合唱温暖感。整体制作在传统前卫摇滚框架内尝试多种风格拼接，注重旋律叙事与器乐对话，歌词由Brad Birzer撰写，带有文学性的浪漫色彩。对于偏爱实验性前卫与即兴的听众而言，这张专辑的跨界融合虽有层次，但更偏向经典prog传统的延伸而非突破性实验。

items.body: Review by XixoTheRock — After dissapearing for some time of social media, Cherc�n has suddenly come back with a single!Which our first sneak peek to their next album, which they have confirmed (via Instagram) that theyare working on.Cherc�n has gone acid rock, and I am enjoying it, a lot if I'm to be honest. The single still hasband's DNA embedded in it, which means it still has a heavy, energetic and vanguardist approachto music, luckily enough, they were able to balance that with good production, something which Icomplained about on my review to their previous LP. Something I'd like to point out is how thissingle is a little more mellow for a hard rock/acid rock track, do I complain? No, that is becausethe music is astounding and hypnotic, and more mature stylistically than their previous work.Something I do not accustom to analyze in my reviews is the cover art, If I'm not mistaken, the lasttime I did so was with "The bedlam on Goliath" by The Mars Volta (which coincidentally, seems to bea big influence for the band, specially Pe�a's vocal delivery). This cover art is an edited pictureof the surface of mars, taken by NASA during their reconnaissance missions during the 70's, it hascirculated the internet and sporadically gotten famous every few years. This picture is without adoubt, fitting for the concept of the track, which orbits around the concept of pareidolia, apsychological phenomenon which consists of the brain triggering pattern recognition and observing(usually) human faces where they are not present. Despite being fitting for the lyrics/concept, I amnot in for taking pre-existing pictures/plastic art works for sleeve art, I consider this practiceto be exhibiting of low initiative, therefore I am not excited about the cover art. Does this takepoints away from the single? Sort of, since cover art does not really impact the composition of thetrack, then I can look over this, but for prog rock, a genre known for it multimedia and grandioseapproach to art, it feels incredibly dissapoiting.Music wise, I consider this single to depart from Cherc�n's previous vanguardist, metal and fusionapproach, taking one which is much closer to acid rock and heavy prog. The track starts with a cleanmath rock guitar riff, the delay and compression being reminiscent of Rush's songs like "RedBarchetta" or "Different strings", being accompanied by a simple bass line, and after Pe�a's vocalsstart, we get our transition to our Hendrix and Rodr�guez L�pez's heavy riffs. The track has somesynthesizer riffs which are played with grace and intricate metrics, which are the the backbone ofthe psychedelic textures, they are slimy spots on our vision which make us feel like we're spinningaround. There are two transposed and dueling saxophones which are the texture that grounds us alittle from our trance to space, the mixture of Synths and Saxophone polymetrics/polyrhythms createa psychedelic eter which makes us feel like we are floating in a dimension of patterns and figureswhich are celestial, supernatural, powerful and colourful. The jarring, clean then heavy then cleanagain guitar riffs are what give the track it's heavy acid rock feel, they are frenetic, much moresimple than Cherc�n's debut album riffs but still quite interesting, specially tonally, they arereminiscent of Tool and The grateful dead in a lot of ways, one of which is it's repetitive butheavy patterns, despite being in 4/4 most of the time, the bass also acts much more like a secondguitar instead of a rhythmic instrument, much like Metallica's original bassit Cliff Burton'sapproach to his instrument. It is the mixture of psychedelic textures with heavier riffs and amoderately energetic drumming which separate this from Avant Garde Fusion metal and drives thesingle towards Acid rock, it is heavy, psychedelic, but yet balanced and soft. The feel o get islike I am swimming in a sea looming over the mysterious auroras of Saturn and it's moons, it'scaptivating and dreamlike, but the energy is what makes this track NOT be a boring mellow space rocktrack, which is what it could have become, controlled frenzy and moderate energy that doesn't reachaggressiveness is what makes this track unique, very much like what Jimi Hendrix would write orplay.I think it'd be redundant to mention the incredible musicianship and dynamic of the musicians, sinceI have already written about this in the past (check my Cherc�n's LP debut review if you areinterested in the Chilean scene!), so I will elaborate further on what improved frok their previousrecord, mistakes they patched. I'd start with the most important thing which is Pe�a's vocals, whichhad been buried previously under layers and layers of loud instrumentation and a very mumble likedelivery, Pe�a finally articulates his vocals much more and this makes it much easier and lessdraining to try to appreciate the lyrics and their relation to the instrumentation, while alsokeeping his energy that accompanies the instrumentation perfectly, his influences by Cedric BixleyZavala have paid off! The production has also improved significantly when compared to their previousrecord, it's much more clear and balanced, less reverberating and recorded with better equipment,this I theorize is due to the new financing and help from organizations such as the Chileangovernment via their ministry of culture. The musicians are already well trained, experimented andvirtuoso so not much more to say regarding this. Does the single have flaws their previous recorddid? I'd say Peña still doesn't articulate to it's fullest yet, despite it all, the single denotes asignificant improvement compared to their previous work.The lyrics certainly are interesting! They are spiritual, very spiritual if I have to be honest,focussing on transcendence from the mundane human body and reaching it's fullest potential, thisexplored through the lens of our relationship to the material world around us. Those who arefamilliarezed with German idealism and Descartes's thought will recognize the resemblances theselyrics have to key concepts of the record, such as the thesis and antithesis Hegel speaks about, orhow Immanuel Kant critiqued pure reason and the idealists thought of how we can't actually accessthe world around us if it's not through perception and subjectivity. This is while the single iscalled "Pareidolia" and why it leaves heavy vanguardism behind for an acid rock approach. I amparticularly fond of the closing line "Elijo el infinito" (I choose infinity), which sums andsynthetices the entire track astonishingly great.Overall, I'd consider this single to be a great example of how to write acid rock in the 21st Centuryand it certainly does promise us a great record from Cherc�n in the near future, leaving an openquestion before us, will Cherc�n be able to top the biggest Chilean prog and art rock bands of thescene with their next record? Only time will tell!

items._cn_summary: Chercón暌违社交媒体多日后回归，发布单曲作为下一张专辑的预尝。乐队此作转向酸摇滚路线，但仍保留了以往前卫、能量充沛且具先锋性的乐队基因，编曲成熟度与制作水准较前作有所提升。评论特别批评封面艺术直接挪用NASA七十年代火星表面照片的做法，认为这在以多媒体宏大叙事著称的进步摇滚领域显得缺乏原创主动性，但在一定程度上仍可接受。音乐层面，作品以清亮的数学摇滚吉他riff开篇，延迟与压缩手法令人联想到Rush的经典段落，随后过渡到受Hendrix与Omar Rodríguez-López影响的重型riff。合成器riff以精致复节奏构建迷幻肌理，两支萨克斯的转调对位与合成器多节奏交织，营造出漂浮于异度空间的听觉体验。

items.body: Belgian synth artist Enzo Kreft has released “Escape Failed”, the second official single from his upcoming 2027 album “Synthetic Future (The Collapse of the Human Domain)”. The track came out on September 4, 2026, as a digital single, alongside an official music video. Escape Failed by Enzo Kreft According to Kreft, “Synthetic Future (The Collapse of the Human Domain)” follows on from his previous album, “Control”, moving from the exercise of power through propaganda, surveillance, and social manipulation toward its aftermath, a reality in which humans are no longer directly oppressed by regimes but instead exist within a system governed by algorithms, synthetic truths, and self-regulating mechanisms. “Escape Failed” describes the moment humanity discovers that escaping that system is no longer possible: apparent freedom of choice turns out to be an illusion, since every move has been predicted and every deviation logged. About Enzo Kreft Enzo Kreft is the project of Belgian artist Eric Vandamme, based in Mechelen. He has released music since 1983, starting with the minimal synth albums “Me Is” (1983) and “Cicatrice” (1984), both recorded with a Korg MS-10, a monophonic Yamaha synthesizer, a Crumar Trilogy keyboard, and early drum machines. His early catalog was reissued and compiled by Walhalla Records in the 2010s, and he has continued to release new albums, including “Turning Point” (2016), “Wasteland” (2017), “Control” (2019), “Different World” (2021), and “Shelter” (2023), followed by the 40th-anniversary compilation “XL” (2023). Side-Line interviewed Kreft in 2021, in “The Future Looks Bright”, and again in 2023, in “You Can’t Be Punk Enough These Days”. “Escape Failed” is his second single from the upcoming “Synthetic Future (The Collapse of the Human Domain)”, due in 2027.
items._cn_summary: 比利时音乐人Enzo Kreft推出新单曲《Escape Failed》，是其2027年专辑《Synthetic Future (The Collapse of the Human Domain)》的第二支官方单曲。作品延续了Kreft自1980年代以来以模拟合成器与早期鼓机为核心的minimal synth路线，主题上承接前作《Control》中关于权力、宣传与社会操控的探讨，转向算法治理下人类失去直接压迫却陷入系统自动调节的后压迫状态。单曲描述人类发现逃离系统已不可能、自由选择成为幻觉的瞬间，强调每个行为都被预测、每个偏差都被记录。文章为唱片新闻稿，侧重专辑概念与艺术家背景，未提供具体声响分析或制作细节，因此音乐本身的创新性、声音设计等信息尚不明确。曲目于2026年9月4日以数字单曲形式发行，并配有官方音乐视频。Kreft的项目由比利时艺术家Eric Vandamme主理，曾以《Me Is》和《Cicatrice》等早期专辑奠定风格，并在近年持续发行新作。该单曲作为概念专辑的引子，适合关注暗潮、实验电子与合成器音乐的听众进一步试听验证。

items.body: TİR, the Sydney-based solo project of Turkish-born multi-instrumentalist Oytun Bektas, will support Mortiis and Nytt Land on the “Southern Ritual” tour of Australia in November 2026. The dates follow two new TİR singles released this year, “Vengeance” and Possessed, streaming below. TİR mixes dungeon synth, dark ambient, cinematic composition and metal-rooted atmosphere into a single project that Bektas writes, records and produces largely on his own. The “Southern Ritual” tour, presented by Hardline Media, runs across four Australian cities: Thursday, November 19, 2026 – Factory Floor, Sydney, NSW Friday, November 20, 2026 – Crowbar, Brisbane, QLD Saturday, November 21, 2026 – Croxton, Melbourne, VIC Sunday, November 22, 2026 – Ed Castle, Adelaide, SA Norwegian artist Mortiis and Siberian duo Nytt Land co-headline the run, with TİR billed as special guest on all four dates. It marks Mortiis’ first Australian shows with a full band and Nytt Land’s Australian debut. Mortiis released the album “Ghosts of Europa” on Prophecy Productions in June 2026, the label also behind the festival where TİR built part of its European following. TİR’s two 2026 singles TİR released “Vengeance” on March 27, 2026, followed by “Possessed” on July 3, 2026, both self-released through Orko Productions and issued on Bandcamp. Bektas wrote, performed and recorded “Vengeance” alone, crediting the cover art to himself, while “Possessed” was composed, performed, arranged, recorded and mixed entirely at Orko Productions in Sydney, with cover photography by Melike Bektas. Both tracks build slowly, layering horn-like synth tones and choral textures over an eight-minute run time on “Possessed” and just under six minutes on “Vengeance.” Possessed by Tir About TİR Oytun Bektas started TİR after moving from Türkiye to Sydney, where the project has been based since. Bandcamp and Rate Your Music list “Mountains” as TİR’s earliest full-length, released in 2016, followed by “Urd, Skuld & Verdandi” and “The Vanished Civilization of Xattoth” in 2019, “Nigritude” in 2020, “Persepolis” in 2021, “Awaiting the Dawn” in 2023 and the single “Sarcophagus” later that year. Orko Productions, the Sydney label and production outfit that mixes and masters TİR’s catalogue, has released the project’s work throughout that period. TİR has toured beyond Australia as well, including a show at Whammy Bar in Auckland, New Zealand, in July 2026, plus dates across Europe. Bektas has described performing at Prophecy Fest in Germany as “one of the most important recent milestones” for TİR. That festival history, along with the shows across Australia, New Zealand and Europe, sets up the “Southern Ritual” tour and the two new singles as the project’s latest chapter.

items._cn_summary: 本文报道了悉尼单人项目TİR将作为特别嘉宾参与Mortiis与Nytt Land的澳大利亚巡演，并重点介绍其2026年发行的两首单曲《Vengeance》和《Possessed》。TİR由土耳其裔多乐器演奏家Oytun Bektas主导，融合了地牢合成器、暗色氛围、电影化配器与金属根源。两首作品均以缓慢铺陈的方式构建，长时长内叠加号角般的合成音色与合唱质感，其中《Possessed》长达八分钟，由Bektas在悉尼Orko Productions工作室独立完成作曲、演奏、录音与混音。文章还梳理了TİR自2016年以来的专辑发行脉络及其在德国Prophecy Fest等地的演出经历，说明其欧洲影响力的积累。整体而言，这是一篇以巡演公告和新单曲发布为核心的新闻稿，对音乐本身的深入评析有限，但足以呈现其融合暗潮与实验性的方向。

items._cn_summary: Tricky时隔六年推出第十五张专辑，邀请同乡新人歌手Mitch Sanders全程担任主唱，自己则退居制作位。整张作品在紧张的听觉氛围中，让安静与躁动相互交织，呈现出平衡而富有推进感的声响结构。不同于前作的悲伤基调，这张专辑更像是在昏暗中一步步走向光明的过程，步伐坚定而有力。制作上的细致处理和人声与节奏的紧密咬合，使作品在情绪与力度之间找到了稳定的支点。

items.body:
Though this recording documents the work of thirteen of Belgium's most innovative ensembles, the real star is the Park Abbey located just outside Leuven and founded in 1129. Built and maintained for the purpose of quiet meditation, the abbey hosted the musicians who used the quiet surroundings to prepare and record their unique musical imaginings. The result is a mostly instrumental collection that mines the riches of Belgian folk and world music traditions, including Romani scales,
La Pump
rhythms, and accordion-based
bal-musette
flavors.
For example, Slovenian-native R�n�lius Bikar�s searing violin opens the set with �R�fuge.� He and his self-named ensemble channel pan-European Roma history.
Meanwhile, �Poor Boy� is a Django Reinhardt-inspired swing tune by Charlotte Pelgen & Bipolar Bows. Pelgen sings in English, and with her ukulele strumming sounding very much like a tenor banjo, the tune is enlivened by Lotte Remmen�s St�phane Grappelli-like fiddle lines.
The distinctive sound of the oud announces yet another musical tradition. Blending Mediterranean with Arabic sounds, the Lebanese-Belgian singer Amber Haddad and her trio, oudist Adil Benhsain and double bassist Martijn Vanbuel, spin a beguiling musical web. According to the liner notes (translated from the Dutch), �Tawazden� is about �seeking balance and finding peace within a complex environment.� Further, �the various spaces of the abbey and their murals are the direct source of inspiration.�
The accordion is especially prominent. So too is the Western classical tradition. Sounding almost Baroque, �Sacristia Invisibilis,� is another standout for me. Here, mandolinist Andries Boone is joined by Anouk Sanczuk on octave violin (sometimes called the baritone violin, tuned an octave lower than standard) and on harpsichord Sandra Van der Gucht. They create an indescribable sound you have to hear.
Throughout, the Abbey�s stone presence looms. Aur�lie Charneux�s solo clarinet piece �L'Ape Millenaria� is about a thousand-year-old bee that haunts the abbey. �Thila,� by Enara Navaira, evokes ancient Celts with a jazzy double bass and drum kit behind throat singing and Citera (a kind of Hungarian zither).
Airboxes is a duo who mix chromatic and diatonic accordions. Their offering �Abdij 1� sounds improvised. Again from the liner notes, �they share their impressions of the timelessness of monastic life.�
Despite the wide range of styles,
The Sound of the Abbey
has a coherence, perhaps informed by the artists� shared inspiration. The record is often surprising and always soothing. Three years in the making, the ensembles were lovingly recorded and mixed by Bert Huysentruyt and mastered by Pieter De Wagter from Equus Mastering. They have rendered a warm sound using the natural reverb of ancient stone provided by the project�s silent partner.

items._cn_summary: 这是一张比利时合辑，十三支乐队在1129年建立的帕克修道院中录制，利用古石建筑的自然混响塑造温暖音色。专辑跨越多种风格：罗姆人小提琴融合泛欧流浪历史，手风琴巴尔穆塞舞曲传统，阿拉伯乌德琴编织地中海与中东音网，曼陀林与羽管键琴组合呈现近似巴洛克质感，还有以中世纪蜜蜂为灵感的独奏单簧管作品。整体以器乐为主，融汇比利时民间与世界音乐元素，强调修道院空间作为共同灵感来源。录制历时三年，由Bert Huysentruyt录制混音，Pieter De Wagter母带处理，保留了古老石墙提供的天然混响。风格偏向跨界融合与民谣传统，虽具一定实验性与文化多样性，但整体氛围偏舒缓冥想，创新性和声音设计的突破性相对有限。

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以跨文化音乐合作为核心，追溯十九世纪墨西哥牛仔前往夏威夷牧牛的历史脉络，将西班牙语与夏威夷语民谣互译改编，融合尤克里里、墨西哥竖琴、手风琴与滑棒吉他等传统乐器。Taj Mahal与David Hidalgo担任核心催化者，与夏威夷本土歌者及乐队成员合作，在加州San Pablo总部一室同期录音完成，保留了强烈的现场即兴感。曲目涵盖老夏威夷歌配新西语词、老墨西哥歌配新夏威夷语词、新创曲及传统美式民谣，编排层次丰富且具有即兴延展。伍迪·格思里的《Deportee》被重新诠释为对移民劳工现实的社论，凸显专辑的社会关怀维度。整体呈现语言、文化、年龄与性别的多元协作理念，是一次融合传统根源与跨太平洋对话的田野式音乐实践。

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了圣多美和普林西比两座小岛在七十至八十年代录制的Puxa舞曲，属于葡萄牙语非洲国家群PALOP音乐传统的一部分。Puxa融合了来自其他前葡萄牙非洲殖民地的节奏元素，同时吸收了merengue、Kompas、Soukouss、Benga等加勒比与非洲邻近地区的律动，形成跨大西洋的音乐对话。评论指出，这种音乐并非纯靠多元素拼贴，而拥有自身独立的传统，曾因葡萄牙殖民禁令而转入地下。合辑共收录十五首曲目，突出多把吉他交织盘旋、鼓手与贝斯及键盘形成律动骨架的结构，演唱以应答式和声融入旋律框架。Pedro Lima、Sangazuza及Africa Negra等乐队展示了节奏层剥落与堆叠时驱动舞者的能力，整张合辑呈现了录音资源匮乏背景下依然蓬勃的岛屿音乐生态。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Sir Richard Bishop继《Hillbilly Ragas》之后的延续之作，由独立厂牌Drag City发行。艺术家作为前Sun City Girls吉他手，延续了对美国民间吉他风格的探索与拓展路线。专辑标题中的'Erotica'带有一定的误导性，曲名如'Hooker's Bend'、'Finger, Tennessee'等实为美国南方某些地区的地名，暗示其音乐根基仍植根于地域文化与地理叙事。整体而言，这是一张在民谣传统框架内进行个人化诠释的吉他作品，延续了艺术家一贯的实验性民谣探索路径，但在类型突破上相对保守，更偏向对既有风格的延伸而非颠覆性创新。

items.body: Purple Trash release their new album “Velvet Nightmares and Cold Sleep” on Swiss Dark Nights. The twelve-track record is out now on digiCD, moving between darkwave, gothic rock, post-punk and electronica. Purple Trash is the solo project of Sergio Da Silva, also known as Bornyhake, a Swiss multi-instrumentalist and composer who has been active on the Swiss underground scene for over twenty-five years and who founded the band Borgne in the 1990s. Da Silva launched Purple Trash in 2020, and “Velvet Nightmares and Cold Sleep” pushes the project deeper into a claustrophobic, self-contained sound, moving between slower, melancholic passages and more electronic, rhythmic territory. Opener “The Echoes of a Sleeping Mind” sets a melancholic tone built around guitar and vocals within its first two minutes, while “Scatterbrain Cathedral” follows with electric guitar and a heavier electronic arrangement. The album’s rhythm section pushes hardest on “It’s a Funeral Pyre”, before “I Tried to Sniff Coffee” returns to a bleaker, more introspective register that runs through the rest of the record. The full tracklist reads “The Echoes of a Sleeping Mind”, “Scatterbrain Cathedral”, “Ashes of Desire”, “I’m Hacking Like a Broke-Down Car”, “Walls Without Names”, “It’s a Funeral Pyre”, “I Tried to Sniff Coffee”, “Chains Made of Gold”, “Through a Forest of Tobacco Trees”, “I Was a Trash Can”, “Feathers in the Shadows” and “A Morning Beyond All Worry”. Velvet Nightmares and Cold Sleep by Purple Trash About Purple Trash Purple Trash is the solo project of Swiss musician Sergio Da Silva, known under the alias Bornyhake, who has been active on the Swiss underground scene for more than twenty-five years. Da Silva founded the band Borgne in the 1990s, entwining ethereal melodies with drum machines. He launched Purple Trash as a solo outlet in 2020, moving between darkwave, gothic rock, post-punk and electronica while keeping the dark, unsettling atmospheres that run through his other work. “Velvet Nightmares and Cold Sleep”, released through Swiss Dark Nights, is his latest album under the Purple Trash name.
items._cn_summary: 瑞士地下场景资深音乐人Sergio Da Silva以Purple Trash之名发行的新专辑在Swiss Dark Nights厂牌下推出。整张作品横跨暗潮、哥特摇滚、后朋克与电子音乐四个领域，呈现出封闭式的阴郁氛围。开场曲以吉他人声奠定忧郁基调，随后的曲目逐步加入更厚重的电子编配；中段节奏密集的曲目构成全专辑最强烈的段落，末段则回到内省的阴暗色调。十二首曲目在缓慢的忧郁段落与电子节奏区域之间交替切换，未见显著的跨界实验或声音设计突破，整体仍属于类型框架内的常规创作。作为独立地下厂牌发行，评论内容偏向新闻性质，缺乏深度乐评分析。

items.body: Tout Debord release “Necrologia”, a 32-track double CD compilation, on Icy Cold Records. The digipak gathers the complete collection of EPs and singles the project released between 2021 and 2026, on labels including Detriti Records, Sierpien Records and Salle d’Attente. Tout Debord is the solo project of Leonid Diaghilev, born in Belarus and based in Paris for several years, who wrote, recorded and mixed every song on “Necrologia” himself. The compilation moves from 80s-inspired coldwave to synthpunk influences drawn from the 2000s, filtered through a lo-fi aesthetic across two discs of sixteen tracks each. A vinyl edition with a shorter tracklist is planned for later in the year. About Tout Debord Tout Debord is the solo project of Leonid Diaghilev, a musician born in Belarus and based in Paris, France. The project’s name fuses the French phrase “tout d’abord” (“first of all”) with a nod to philosopher and Situationist Guy Debord. Since starting the project in Paris in 2020, Diaghilev has released a string of EPs and singles across several independent labels, drawing on the early albums of The Cure and industrial synthpop acts such as Fad Gadget and Depeche Mode, alongside the French cold wave scene of the 1980s. “Necrologia”, released through Icy Cold Records, collects that catalogue on a single double-disc release for the first time.

items.body: Review by Grumpyprogfan — On my first listen this album resonated with me instantly. After several more listens it only gets better, and from all the great music released this year, "Quube" may be my album of the year. The music rocks, swings, has soulful passages and is somewhat catchy all at the same time. The lineup for "Quube" is - Chad Wackerman (drums), Alex Machacek (guitar), Jimmy Haslip (bass), and Steve Hunt (keys). Every song is engaging and if you know these players, there is no surprise that the musicianship is out of this world. If you're familiar with Chad's previous solo albums there is a high probability you will love this. So far this is only available digitally, but it sounds amazing thanks to Steve Hunt and the group. Highly recommend to fusion fans.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张以鼓手为核心的四重奏融合爵士专辑，由Chad Wackerman领衔，联合吉他手Alex Machacek、贝斯手Jimmy Haslip和键盘手Steve Hunt共同完成。整张专辑在摇滚律动与摇摆节奏之间自由切换，穿插灵魂乐式的段落铺垫，部分旋律线带有较强的记忆点。评论者经过反复聆听后认为，乐手们的高水准演奏贯穿始终，每一首曲目都保持足够的吸引力。录音品质出色，仅以数字形式发行，声音清晰度令人满意。作为一张以乐器演奏为主的融合爵士作品，它更侧重演奏技巧的展示和类型内部的成熟表达，而非实验性突破或跨领域融合。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — Despite the fact that this is a reunion album in which the band performs cover versions of it's old material, it's always nice to hear Quidam music--and to hear them reunited with former founding lead singer Emilia Nazaruk (n�e Derkowska) is a real treat--even these 30 years later. The other founding members present from that wonderful first album from 1996 are guitarist Maciej Meller and keyboard maestro Zbigniew Florek--the two dudes who have been writing the bulk of the band's music since day one. My favorite song straight away is the gorgeous "Jesteś (w labiryncie myśli) / You Are (in the Labyrinth of Thoughts)"--a song in which Emilia proves how she's still got all the skills and talents that she put on display back in 1996. "One Day We Find" also avails itself with great power as Bartosz Kossowicz earns his place among the pantheon of great Polish prog vocalists.The album's best song, however, may be its beautiful finale: "Spotykanie" (7:32) Here we have a remake of a song that first appeared on the band's last previous album, 2012's Saiko. I always love it when Quidam (or any band from non-English speaking countries) sings in their native tongue. Here Bartosz and Emilia take turns and even back one another as well as dueting within a gorgeous soundscape of guitars, synth washes, piano chords, and lilting flute melodies over Mariusz and Maciej Wr�blewski's warm and comforting bed of hypnotic rhythms. Then there's Maciej Meller's wonderful soaring guitar solo in the sixth and seventh minutes before Bartosz, Emilia, and Zbigniew so delicately tuck us in (for a wonderful night of peaceful sleep). Bravissimo! Great ending song to a fine comeback album! (14.125/15)Bass player Mariusz Zi�łkowski continues doing his great job of filling the shoes of the band's previous bassists as does flutist Jacek Zasada filling an equally-important role to this band's traditional sound. It's so nice to have Quidam back and still going strong!
items._cn_summary: 波兰乐队Quidam的重组专辑，重新演绎早期经典曲目。创始主唱Emilia Nazaruk回归，与原始吉他手Maciej Meller和键盘手Zbigniew Florek重聚。专辑亮点包括波兰语演唱的"Jesteś (w labiryncie myśli)"展现主唱声线功力，终曲"Spotykanie"以原声吉他、合成器铺底、钢琴和弦与长笛旋律交织，营造温暖催眠的节奏底色，第六至第七分钟Maciej Meller的吉他独奏盘旋上升，最终三人合声温柔收束全篇。整体延续乐队九十年代以来的传统声响：键盘主导的器乐架构、长笛点缀与人声交织的欧洲前卫摇滚脉络。

items.body: ShiShi, the dark electronic project of Ljubljana-based artist Artur Ziganshin, released a music film on 1 September 2026. Titled “Blood Tape”, the 5:14 film is not a single or an album. Ziganshin wrote and directed it himself, and it is connected to his 2025 EP of the same name. The film uses vampirism as a metaphor for dependency. It follows a character whose private need gradually takes over his voice and identity. Ziganshin described the film’s arc as one where “fear becomes invitation,” invitation becomes hunger, and hunger “learns to speak in your voice.” The film is structured in six parts: Fear, Invitation, Hunger, Possession, Withdrawal and Void. “Blood Tape” was shot at 3840 x 2160 resolution and 24fps. Ziganshin handles the film credits himself: written and performed by Artur Ziganshin, with music and lyrics also credited to ShiShi. The film connects directly to the “Blood Tape” EP, a four-track release ShiShi put out in 2025 that includes the title track “Blood Tape” alongside “Doomnight,” “Rocket Ship to Hell” and “Storm Clouds Gather.” The film takes its title, and its central metaphor, from that release. About ShiShi ShiShi is the dark electronic project of Artur Ziganshin, an artist based in Ljubljana, Slovenia, who works across music and film. The project pairs original songs with visual work built around themes of fear, dependency, memory and transformation. Ziganshin writes, performs and directs the project’s output himself. Before “Blood Tape,” ShiShi released music including “Madness was Sad,” “Black birds” and “Sodium Crown.” In 2025, ShiShi released the “Blood Tape” EP, a set of tracks exploring dependency and confession through dense, cinematic electronic production. The 2026 “Blood Tape” film extends that EP’s world into a standalone visual narrative, translating its central metaphor of addiction as vampirism into a six-part cinematic structure.
items._cn_summary: 斯洛文尼亚卢布尔雅那艺术家ShiShi发布音乐电影《Blood Tape》，全长5分14秒，以吸血鬼为隐喻探讨依赖与身份消解的主题。影片由艺术家Artur Ziganshin自编自导，自演并独立完成音乐与歌词创作，延续其2025年同名EP的世界观。该EP包含四首曲目，以密集的电影化电子制作探索依赖与忏悔。影片结构分为六个部分：恐惧、邀请、饥饿、附身、戒断与虚无，拍摄规格为3840×2160分辨率24fps。ShiShi的音乐横跨黑暗电子与电影配乐领域，主题聚焦恐惧、依赖、记忆与蜕变，作品以视觉叙事与声音设计的结合为核心特色，将上瘾机制转化为吸血鬼化的六段式电影结构。

Claudio Simonetti, Fabio Pignatelli and Massimo Mo
items.body: Claudio Simonetti’s Goblin reissue the “Tenebre” soundtrack on 18 September 2026 through Rustblade. The label presses a limited yellow smoke vinyl LP restricted to 499 copies, packaged with a replica of the original Italian cinema poster, alongside a digiCD edition that adds six bonus tracks. “Tenebre” is the score for Dario Argento’s 1982 film of the same name, known internationally as “Tenebrae”. Claudio Simonetti, Fabio Pignatelli and Massimo Morante, the three Goblin members behind the soundtrack, originally released it on the Italian label Cinevox in 1982. The score mixes early-1980s electronic dance and Italo disco elements with horror-driven progressive rock, built on vocoder vocals, electronic drums and pulsating basslines. The vinyl LP carries the original eight-track program: “Tenebre”, “Gemini”, “Slow Circus” and “Lesbo” on side A, then “Flashing”, “Tenebre (Reprise)”, “Waiting the Death” and “Jane Mirror Theme” on side B. The digiCD keeps that sequence and adds six further tracks, including a remix of “Flashing” by TIBIA and a cover of “Waiting the Death” by Simulakrum Lab, alongside alternate and live versions. Tenebre – Soundtrack by Claudio Simonetti’s Goblin About Claudio Simonetti’s Goblin Goblin formed in Italy in the mid-1970s around keyboardist Claudio Simonetti, guitarist Massimo Morante, bassist Fabio Pignatelli and drummer Walter Martino, after working under the names Oliver and Cherry Five. The band took the name Goblin while scoring Dario Argento‘s film “Profondo Rosso” (“Deep Red”) in 1975, and the soundtrack, released on Cinevox, established the group as Argento’s regular composers. Goblin went on to score Argento’s “Suspiria” in 1977 and, working with director George A. Romero, the soundtrack for “Dawn of the Dead” in 1978, released under the title “Zombi”. For “Tenebre” in 1982, Simonetti, Pignatelli and Morante reunited to compose the score, again for an Argento film and again released on Cinevox. Simonetti has continued to perform and re-record the band’s soundtrack catalogue under the name Claudio Simonetti’s Goblin, and has worked repeatedly with Rustblade on reissues and repackagings of the Argento-era scores, including the label’s past editions of the “Profondo Rosso” soundtrack. The new “Tenebre” vinyl and digiCD editions add to that reissue history with the film’s original score in a limited pressing.
items._genre: progressive rock / electronic / italo disco / soundtrack
items._cn_summary: 这是Claudio Simonetti's Goblin对1982年Dario Argento同名电影《Tenebre》配乐的再版发行，由Rustblade推出限量499张的黄烟胶LP和附带六首加曲的digiCD。原配乐融合了早期1980年代电子舞曲、Italo disco元素与恐怖电影驱动的前卫摇滚，以声码器人声、电子鼓和脉动贝斯构建出标志性的声响。LP保留原始八轨曲目，digiCD则加入TIBIA的“Flashing”混音、Simulakrum Lab对“Waiting the Death”的翻唱以及现场和替代版本。作为Goblin成员为Argento创作的经典配乐，它体现了乐队在恐怖片音乐中将合成器音色与摇滚张力结合的成熟手法，也是前卫摇滚与早期电子舞曲交汇的典型样本。此次再版通过额外曲目和限量载体为乐迷提供了更完整的收藏版本。

items.body: Pet Shop Boys will release “A Man From The Future”, an eight-part work about British mathematician and codebreaker Alan Turing, on 9 October 2026 via Parlophone Records. Neil Tennant and Chris Lowe created the piece with Turing biographer Professor Andrew Hodges, and it can be pre-ordered now in several formats. The composition was first performed at the BBC Proms in July 2014 at London’s Royal Albert Hall, with the BBC Concert Orchestra, the BBC Singers and narration by actor Juliet Stevenson. For this new recording, both the text and the music have been revised and rearranged. Pet Shop Boys produced the album together with composer Sven Helbig, who also arranged the strings and vocals. The recording, made in the UK and Germany over the past year, features the Manchester Camerata Octet on strings and the Manchester Grammar School Choir, with Stevenson again narrating. The album is structured in eight parts following episodes in Turing’s life and work: “Natural wonders every child should know”, “He dreamed of machines”, “The Enigma”, “Other ranks”, “The memory and the control”, “The trial”, “Only in his death” and “A man from the future”. It will be released on vinyl, as a 2CD set and on Blu-ray audio, with the Blu-ray edition carrying the full sung-and-narrated version, an instrumental version and a version without narration in Dolby Atmos and 96kHz/24-bit stereo. Ahead of the release, BBC Radio 6 Music gives the new recording its broadcast on Sunday 4 October within Stuart Maconie’s “Freak Zone” (8-10pm), where Maconie also talks to Tennant, Lowe and Hodges about the reworking. The piece airs again that night on BBC Radio 3’s “Unclassified” (11.30pm-12.30am), with Tennant, Lowe and Hodges joining presenter Elizabeth Alker. Both broadcasts stay on BBC Sounds for 30 days. On 8 October, Tennant, Lowe and Hodges appear at the Imperial War Museum North in Manchester for a listening and conversation event built around a full playback of the album. About Pet Shop Boys Pet Shop Boys formed in London in 1981, when Neil Tennant, then a journalist at Smash Hits, met keyboardist Chris Lowe in a Chelsea electronics shop. The duo built up material through the early 1980s, first from Tennant’s flat and later in a small Camden Town studio, developing songs that became “West End Girls”, “It’s a Sin” and “Rent”. “West End Girls” reached number one in the UK and US in 1986, launching a run of albums – “Please” (1986), “Actually” (1987), “Introspective” (1988), “Behaviour” (1990) and beyond – built on Tennant’s deadpan vocals, Lowe’s electronic productions and lyrics that mixed pop hooks with social observation. Across four decades, Pet Shop Boys have continued to release studio albums, tour internationally and score stage and film work, including “Battleship Potemkin” and the musical “Closer to Heaven”. They are currently on their “Dreamworld” tour, for which Side-Line previously covered the announcement of the German support acts. “A Man From The Future” marks the duo’s first dedicated concept work built around a single historical figure, revisiting a piece they first performed with Andrew Hodges in 2014 and now releasing as a studio album on Parlophone.
items._cn_summary: 这是一篇关于Pet Shop Boys新专辑《A Man From The Future》的发行新闻稿，而非实质性乐评。作品以八段结构讲述数学家艾伦·图灵的生平，结合电子合成器、管弦乐与合唱，并保留朱丽叶·史蒂文森的旁白。音乐由乐队与作曲家Sven Helbig联合制作，由曼彻斯特卡梅拉塔八重奏和曼彻斯特文法学校合唱团录制，呈现古典与电子融合的跨界形态。文本基于图灵传记作者安德鲁·霍奇斯的合作修订，并提供了多种音频版本。尽管题材严肃且采用管弦乐编制，整体仍属于流行电子框架内的艺术化尝试，缺乏尖锐的实验性声音设计。作为主流厂牌下的商业发行，其创新程度有限，但题材选择和历史叙事具有一定独特性。

items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. Find the artist online. Sara Serpa - Encounters and Collisions (Review) Karine Polwart- Laws of Motion (Review) Live in the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, 2025

items.body: Sudan Dudan is a Norwegian duo, Marit Karlberg and Anders Erik R�ine, who have released four albums over the last twenty years. On M�rke refrenger , their fifth, they are joined by Hans Hulb�kmo and Magnus Skavhaug Nergaard, contributing instrumentally and with the production. There are eight songs on the album with accompaniment principally led by acoustic guitar, augmented by fiddles, langeleik, lyre, jaws harp and more. The opening track, �Gard og grind� (�Fence and gate�) is a fine introduction to what is to come: finger-picked acoustic guitar, fiddle, bass and snare-drum played with brushes leading into the harmonized vocal, together creating an alluring sound drawing the listener in. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The mood of the album, reflected in its title which translates as �Dark Refrains,� is not always dark, but most of the material, including the title track, certainly has a reflective quality. According to the press release �the lyrics smoulder with unease about the present and the future, while looking back to the myths and riddles of the past. They speak of the earth, the sun, the moon, stars and planets, of lost brothers, quarrelling sisters, loss and grief, of the power of imagination, and of the answers to the simplest and most difficult riddles.� The lyrics of all the songs, in Norwegian, are included in the sleeve notes and while a hasty online translation can aid with some understanding, the full meanings tend to remain cryptic, but there is a sense that words and music complement each other. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan For all its dark moodiness, M�rke refrenger does have its lighter moments. �Bagatelle� recalls and reinvents the melody of a well-known French song, adding some off-kilter harmonies, while �Rulleball� is more characteristically Norwegian, employing a vocal style known as tralling in which words are replaced by a vocalization of the melody, originally used to accompany dances when no instrument was available. No translation necessary there. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The final track �Skriften p� veggen� (�the writing on the wall�) features, for the only time on the album, electric guitar. The sound is deep and twangy, shades of Duane Eddy or a David Lynch soundtrack and it works very well. All in all a fine, imaginatively conceived and beautifully produced record, available as a download or vinyl. Find the artists online. items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

Vanishment
(Review)

Genuine Negro Jig
(Review)

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑并非传统意义上的音乐作品，而是由录音师Ian Brennan在芝加哥枪支暴力频发的社区现场采集的口述录音集。参与者的年龄从十七岁到六十七岁不等，许多人曾是暴力的受害者或施害者，甚至两者兼具。录音发生在一栋位于南城区的房屋前廊，正值特朗普下令国民警卫队进驻该城的同一天。文中强调了参与者对当地历史的提及，包括Muddy Waters等布鲁斯传奇人物的发源地背景。一位失去两个儿子的长者在讲述过程中情绪崩溃，反复道歉，但作者指出真正应受责备的是社会结构性不公。所有收益将捐赠给致力于以公共卫生方式终结暴力的Cure Violence Global组织。这是一次以声音档案形式呈现的社会田野记录，不含音乐添加，完全由环境声和人声构成。
